newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peasant leader walks free from jail.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peasant leader walks free from jail.

text.p: A Mexican judge has freed one of the leaders of a left-wing peasant movement imprisoned since July on charges of insurrection and sabotage, justice officials said on Friday.
The move deals a blow to official attempts to link the peasant group to left-wing EPR guerrillas in Mexico's impoverished Guerrero state.

Officials said a district judge Thursday overturned a prison sentence handed down in February to Hilario Mesino Acosta, a founding member of the powerful Peasant Organisation in the Southern Mountains (OCSS).
The decision was believed to have been based on a lack of evidence.
Arrested in Mexico City on July 3, 1996, Mesino was held in a jail in the Pacific resort of Acapulco.

Together with OCSS co-founder Benigo Guzman Martinez, Mesino was accused of having ties to EPR guerrillas. But in an interview after his release he said he had always acted within the limits of the law.
